studies.Reference: Greater vegetable and fruit intake is associated with a lower risk of breast cancer among Chinese women.
studies.Authors: Zhang CX, Ho SC, Chen YM, Fu JH, Cheng SZ, Lin FY
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary intake was assessed by face-to-face interviews using a validated food frequency questionnaire.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Four hundred and thirty-eight cases were frequency matched to 438 controls
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The ORs of the highest quartile relative to the lowest quartile of ... watermelon/papaya/cantaloupe were all inversely and significantly related with breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Consumption of ... watermelon/papaya/cantaloupe were all inversely and significantly related with breast cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.p_value: Computed from the reported effect and 95% CI using a normal approximation: p=0.005.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The ORs of the highest quartile relative to the lowest quartile ... 0.53 (95% CI 0.34-0.82)
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Consumption of individual vegetable and fruit groups such as ... watermelon/papaya/cantaloupe
